html:
Directory and shared navigation flows

Directory provides a readable view of the Controller's registered routes and curated page links. Shared navigation gives Directory, Settings, Inference and the Manual consistent disclosure behavior without making navigation a settings save or task action. The UI tour explains the controls. This page traces the source owners and their limits.

From application routes to a readable inventory

flowchart TD App[Current FastAPI top-level routes] --> Filter[Exclude pathless entries and recognized static paths] Filter --> Project[Project path, methods, group and endpoint name] Metadata[Curated primary-page labels and manual IDs] --> Project Docstring[Endpoint docstring first nonempty line] --> Project Project --> Routes[Sorted route inventory and groups] Routes --> Presence[Match curated pages by registered path] Metadata --> Presence Presence --> Pages[Primary cards with route_present] Inference[Registered inference route] -.-> Pages Port[Validated manual port hint] --> Payload[Directory JSON] Routes --> Payload Pages --> Payload Payload --> Browser[Local filtering and literal-text rendering]

directory.py owns the curated metadata and _directory_payload. The core routes serve /directory and expose the JSON at /api/agent/directory. directory.html supplies the shell and loads shared session, navigation, API, error and Manual-link helpers before directory.js uses them. The authenticated app boundary owns access to these surfaces.

The inventory reads app.routes directly. It excludes entries without a path, static mounts containing /static, and /agent-ui/static paths. Other mounts are single entries; it does not recursively enumerate mounted applications. Route methods omit HEAD/OPTIONS; recognized WebSocket routes get a WEBSOCKET marker. Groups are Agent API, compatibility, OpenAPI, WebSocket and utility, sorted by the declared group order and path. Repeated paths for different route registrations can remain separate rows; primary-page lookup uses the path map.

Titles and summaries prefer curated page metadata. Otherwise the summary uses the endpoint's first nonempty docstring line, then a path-derived fallback. Those docstrings are runtime-visible data: developer explanations added as adjacent comments do not change the inventory's public wording. The module also exports shared settings/scheduling namespace constants and numeric coercion helpers; those helpers return bounded values without saving settings.

Curated primary pages remain in the response even when no matching local route exists. route_present: false produces an Unavailable badge for local pages; it does not remove or disable their links. The external Manual card intentionally does not require a Controller route. Inference is inserted only when /inference is registered. This is a registration inventory, not a health probe, permission catalog or promise that every URL accepts a browser GET.

Loading, local search and links

sequenceDiagram participant Page as Directory page participant Shared as Shared API adapter participant Route as Directory route participant App as App route registry participant Nav as Navigation controller Page->>Nav: Mount inline route groups Page->>Shared: Read /api/agent/directory once Shared->>Route: Authenticated no-store GET Route->>App: Inspect top-level routes and metadata App-->>Route: Current registrations alt Read succeeds Route-->>Page: Pages, groups and manual-port hint Page->>Page: Resolve links and render literal-text rows Page->>Nav: Refresh groups and search expansion Page->>Page: Mark ready and remove boot overlay else Read fails Shared-->>Page: Shared response/transport error Page->>Page: Show unavailable status and remove boot overlay end loop User edits Search paths Page->>Page: Filter loaded data by lowercase substring Page->>Nav: Apply temporary matching group IDs end Note over Page,App: Search issues no inventory request or endpoint invocation

The normal read uses SMTOAgentUi.apiJson('/directory'); its API-prefix helper targets /api/agent/directory. The retained fallback uses the shared error-aware fetch/read helpers directly. Success stores page/group arrays and the manual port, renders them and removes the boot overlay. Failure shows a status message and also removes that overlay. There is no polling, automatic retry or live route subscription in this page; reload obtains another inventory.

Search is a trimmed, case-insensitive substring match over loaded metadata. Primary cards include title, path, summary and Manual-link titles; route rows also include group label, endpoint name and methods. Empty search shows everything. Rendering reconstructs rows with text nodes, then reapplies group preferences. The page's page/route counts remain totals of the loaded inventory, not counts of visible search matches. Empty results have separate primary-path and route messages.

Route anchors perform ordinary browser navigation. For a template such as /api/agent/native/{request_id}, the helper merely strips braces, yielding a placeholder-name link; it does not select an actual request ID. Method badges describe the registered API, and clicking a POST-only route does not issue its POST. Use the API's documented inputs and authentication for actual operations.

Manual pills use stable document IDs and open a separate tab with opener isolation. The normal path delegates through agent_ui_shared.js to manual_links.js. That resolver owns bundled/local/public deployment selection and encoded document fragments. Directory's standalone fallback uses current protocol/host plus the reported port. The server port hint accepts integers 1–65535, otherwise 8013. Resolving a link neither fetches a document nor verifies listener availability.

Saved collapse choices versus temporary reveal

sequenceDiagram participant User as User participant Group as Native details element participant Nav as Navigation controller participant Session as Tab session preference owner User->>Group: Activate summary by click, Enter or Space Group->>Nav: Click before native toggle Nav->>Session: Save intended collapsed key for this surface/group Group->>Group: Native activation toggles open opt Search or filter changes Nav->>Session: Read saved collapsed keys Nav->>Group: Open matching groups temporarily Note over Nav,Session: No preference write for search expansion end opt Search clears or rows rebuild Nav->>Session: Read saved collapsed keys Nav->>Group: Refresh from explicit choices and current search end opt Caller reveals an active or deep-linked target Nav->>Group: Unhide target and open nearest group Note over Nav,Session: Reveal preserves the saved collapse choice end

navigation_groups.js creates native details/summary groups and mounts one controller per root in a WeakMap. It queries current child groups when refreshing, so replacing Directory rows does not leave it attached to obsolete nodes. createGroup begins open; refresh applies saved state afterward.

Only explicit summary activation writes navigation_collapsed_groups, keyed by surface:group, through ui_session_state.js. That owner validates and deduplicates at most 64 keys with a combined 2,048-character limit. It keeps allowed preferences in sessionStorage and can retain current-page choices in memory if storage fails. These are tab-session navigation choices, not shared server settings, conversation drafts or permission state.

setSearchMatches(ids) temporarily opens matching groups; null ends that search override, while an empty set represents an active search with no matching groups. reveal(target) unhides a contained target and opens its nearest group without writing a preference. Opening a menu also preserves a collapsed active group and can focus its summary. The caller owns which rows are filtered and when to reveal an active destination. A later refresh can restore the saved collapse choice.

One panel across desktop and narrow layouts

sequenceDiagram participant User as User participant Trigger as Sections button participant Nav as Navigation controller participant Panel as Existing navigation panel participant Dialog as Native modal dialog User->>Trigger: Open Sections on narrow viewport Trigger->>Nav: openMenu() Nav->>Dialog: Move existing panel into dialog body Nav->>Panel: Unhide same DOM nodes Nav->>Dialog: showModal() Nav->>Panel: Focus visible active item or collapsed summary alt Close, Escape or outside click User->>Nav: Close menu Nav->>Dialog: close() Nav->>Panel: Restore beside original placeholder and hide on narrow screen Nav->>Trigger: Restore focus when requested else Viewport becomes desktop Nav->>Dialog: Close without forcing trigger focus Nav->>Panel: Restore home, show panel and retain useful focus Nav->>Trigger: Hide trigger end Note over Nav,Panel: Reparenting preserves the same nodes, listeners and disclosure state

The optional menu configuration creates a labelled native dialog and a comment placeholder at the panel's original location. Opening on a narrow viewport moves the existing panel into that dialog; it does not clone navigation or refetch data. Focus prefers the visible current item, its summary when collapsed, the first visible summary, then Close. Native modal behavior supplies focus containment. Closing restores the panel beside the placeholder and normally returns narrow focus to the trigger. Escape and outside clicks use the same close path.

Breakpoint changes restore the desktop panel or hide it behind the narrow trigger, keeping focus on a visible element where possible. Settings and Inference use the default 980-pixel breakpoint. The Manual passes 820. Directory supplies no menu configuration, so its route groups stay inline at narrow widths; menu methods are no-ops there. Destination selection and closing after a selection belong to each caller, not to the shared group's click handler.

The controller's listeners and optional dialog last for the page lifetime; there is no explicit destroy API. Repeated mounting of the same root returns the first controller and does not replace its options. It assumes valid root/session helpers and stable valid group IDs from its callers.

Implementation and validation boundaries

The Settings integration, Inference integration and Manual integration pass their surface/menu options and own active-link reveal, filtering and destination focus. This guide reviews those navigation call sites, not their complete editors, inference operations or Manual rendering pipelines. Appearance and tooltip implementation remain separate.

Route/asset tests and current-help checks cover Directory entry points and stable Manual IDs. The navigation browser fixture uses isolated API stores across all four shells to check explicit collapse, reload, temporary search/deep-link reveal, responsive focus and absence of preference writes to the backend. These checks do not prove that every listed route accepts GET, that external listeners are running or that an inventory is complete beyond the app's top-level registrations.
